title.rendered: Cambridge IGCSE Biology: Syllabus, Grading & Resources

content.rendered:
Key Summary

  • One Syllabus, Two Tiers: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610) splits into Core and Extended, and your tier sets the papers you sit and the top grade you can earn.
  • Three Papers Each: Every student takes three papers, a multiple choice, a theory paper, and either a practical test or its written alternative.
  • Human Biology Focus: The course leans towards human biology, and strong marks come from precise definitions and clear diagrams.
  • Free Official Resources: Cambridge publishes the syllabus, past papers, mark schemes, examiner reports, and specimen papers, and the coursebook answers sit free on Cambridge GO.
  • Support Built On The Real Paper: Ignite helps Dubai students revise around the actual 0610 structure, not a generic checklist.

Biology looks like the science you can simply memorise. Learn the definitions, label the diagrams, and the marks follow. Then Paper 4 arrives with a data question about an experiment you have never seen, and that idea falls apart fast.

This guide clears up what Cambridge IGCSE Biology actually asks of you. You will see how the syllabus is built, how the six papers fit together, how grading works, which coursebook to trust, and where to find every official past paper. 

At Ignite Training Institute, we work through 0610 with Dubai students every term, so the advice here is practical rather than generic. Knowing the shape of the course early changes how you revise, so let us start with what the qualification is.

What Is Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610)?

Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610) is an international science qualification from Cambridge Assessment International Education, graded A* to G. It covers 21 topics with an emphasis on human biology, and every student sits three papers: a multiple choice paper, a theory paper, and either a practical test or its written alternative.

The course runs on a two-year cycle in most Dubai schools, with students finishing at the end of Year 11. The current version is for exams in 2026, 2027, and 2028, and Cambridge confirmed there are no significant teaching changes from the previous cycle, so recent resources still hold. It sits at the same level as a UK GCSE and feeds directly into AS and A Level Biology.

Core Vs Extended: Which Tier Fits You?

The split between Core and Extended is the first real decision in this subject. Core covers the foundation content and caps at grade C. Extended adds the Supplement material on top of the Core, opens up grades A* to C, and is the route most Dubai students take when aiming for competitive sixth form or university places.

You cannot mix the two. A Core student sits Paper 1 and Paper 3; an Extended student sits Paper 2 and Paper 4. Your teacher usually decides the tier based on your progress, so if you are unsure which papers you are entered for, ask early. It is the single most useful question you can ask this term, because it changes what you revise.

For families comparing exam boards before this stage, our overview of British curriculum tutoring options across the UAE gives useful background.

Know More About: What Is Cambridge Curriculum In UAE? Everything To Know

Cambridge IGCSE Biology Syllabus: What You Study

The Cambridge IGCSE Biology syllabus is broad. It runs across 21 topics, from cell structure to genetic modification, and that breadth is the main reason students feel stretched. The upside is that marks are spread widely, so a solid grasp of the core topics protects your grade even if one area feels weak.

Every topic has Core content that all students learn. Extended students study the same topics but add the Supplement material, which goes deeper rather than introducing separate subjects. The table below lists the 21 official topics and shows what the Supplement adds for Extended students.

The 2026 To 2028 Syllabus Update

The current 0610 syllabus is version 2, published December 2025, for exams in 2026, 2027, and 2028. Cambridge states there are no significant changes that affect teaching, and textbooks endorsed from 2023 remain suitable. So if you already have recent notes or a current coursebook, they still apply. Always check you are using the syllabus for the exact year of your exam, since Cambridge reviews these on a cycle.

Know More About: Why Choose Cambridge? Key Reasons & Benefits

Cambridge IGCSE Biology Exam Papers Explained

Every Cambridge IGCSE Biology student sits three papers, not six. The six paper numbers exist so Cambridge can offer two tiers plus a practical choice, but you only ever take the three that match your route.

So a Core student sits Papers 1, 3, and either 5 or 6. An Extended student sits Papers 2, 4, and either 5 or 6. The theory paper carries the most weight at 50 percent, which is where most of your revision time should go.

Marks are split across three assessment objectives: knowledge and understanding at 50 percent, handling information and problem solving at 30 percent, and experimental skills at 20 percent. That problem-solving share is why pure memorisation stalls around a C. The higher grades come from applying what you know to unfamiliar data.

Paper 5 Vs Paper 6: How Practical Skills Are Tested

Both practical papers test the same experimental skills and the same objective. The difference is format. Paper 5 is a hands-on Practical Test of 1 hour 15 minutes, done in a school laboratory. Paper 6 is a written Alternative to Practical of 1 hour, where you answer questions about experiments without carrying them out.

Your school decides which one you sit, so this is not your choice. Either way, the skills are identical: planning an investigation, identifying variables, recording results in a clear table, plotting graphs, and spotting sources of error. Common contexts include food tests, osmosis, enzyme reactions, photosynthesis rate, and transpiration. Practising these under exam conditions matters as much as learning the theory.

Know More About: IGCSE Exam Dates 2026: Cambridge, Edexcel, And Oxford AQA

How Cambridge IGCSE Biology Is Graded?

Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610) is graded on the A* to G scale, where A* is the top result and G is the lowest classified grade. Your three papers combine into one overall grade based on their weightings, so the 50 percent theory paper carries the most influence.

Your tier sets your ceiling. Core students sit Papers 1 and 3 and can be awarded grades C to G. Extended students sit Papers 2 and 4 and are eligible for the full A* to G range. This is why the Core or Extended decision matters so much: a Core entry cannot reach a B or an A, whatever the mark.

Here is how the A* to G scale works for 0610, and which grades each tier can reach:

These descriptions are a general guide only, since the exact mark for each grade is set fresh every series, as explained below.

A*-G Vs 9-1: The 0610 & 0970 Question

Cambridge offers this subject in two versions. Code 0610 is graded A* to G, and code 0970 is graded 9 to 1. The subject content, papers, and structure are the same; only the grading scale and code differ. Your school enters you for one or the other, and the two cannot be taken in the same exam series. Most Dubai schools use 0610, so check your statement of entry if you are unsure.

One point on grade boundaries: they are not fixed. Cambridge sets the mark needed for each grade after every series, once examiners see how students performed on that specific paper. So a raw mark that earns an A in one session might land differently in another. Always work from the official boundary table for your exact series rather than a rule of thumb like seventy percent.

Know More About: IGCSE Grades Explained: Grading System, Pass Marks 2026

Cambridge IGCSE Biology Coursebook & Where To Find Answers

The most widely used resource is the official Cambridge coursebook. The current edition is the fourth, written by Mary Jones and Geoff Jones and published by Cambridge University Press for examination from 2023. It is endorsed by Cambridge, which means it is matched to the 0610 syllabus, and it remains suitable for the 2026 to 2028 cycle.

A common search is for the coursebook answers. The honest answer is that you do not need a pirated PDF. Cambridge publishes the answers to the coursebook questions free on its Cambridge GO platform, which you reach with the code inside the book or through your school. That is the legitimate source, and it is more reliable than the scattered copies floating around online.

The Jones coursebook is not the only option. Collins and other publishers produce their own endorsed student books, and a workbook and practical workbook sit alongside the Cambridge series for extra practice. Whichever you use, treat the coursebook as your knowledge base and pair it with real past papers for exam technique. A book alone will not prepare you for the way questions are actually asked.

Know More About: IGCSE Subjects: Full List & How To Choose Them?

How To Use Cambridge IGCSE Biology Past Papers

Past papers are the single most useful revision tool for this subject, and Cambridge makes recent ones free. The reliable source is the official 0610 past papers page, where you can download question papers and mark schemes by series. For the current cycle, work with papers from 2023 onwards, since those match the syllabus you are sitting.

Work them properly. Attempt a paper under timed conditions, then mark it yourself against the official mark scheme. Biology mark schemes reward specific words, so comparing your answer to the exact wording examiners accept is where the real learning happens. Descriptive questions worth four or five marks often list more accepted points than there are marks available, so precise vocabulary lifts your score.

What Examiner Reports Tell You (And How To Use Them)

Examiner reports are the most underused free resource Cambridge publishes. After each series, the principal examiner writes up where students commonly lost marks, which questions were misread, and which topics were answered poorly. Reading two or three of these before your mocks tells you, in the board’s own words, what strong answers look like. It is one of the fastest ways to move a grade, and almost no student bothers.

Why Specimen Papers Matter For The 2026 Syllabus

Specimen papers show the current question style when past papers in the exact format are limited. Cambridge publishes them on the main 0610 qualification page alongside the syllabus. They are useful for seeing how the paper is laid out and what the command words expect, so you walk into the exam recognising the format rather than meeting it cold.

Know More About: How To Study For IGCSE Biology: A Complete Guide

How To Study And Revise For Cambridge IGCSE Biology?

Revision works best when it matches the paper, not a generic list. Break the subject into what the exam actually tests: recalling precise definitions, explaining processes, and applying knowledge to unfamiliar data. Each needs a different kind of practice.

Build your revision around a few habits that fit how this subject is marked:

  • Learn key definitions in their exact wording, because Biology mark schemes reward precise terms over rough paraphrases.
  • Test yourself with active recall and past-paper questions instead of re-reading notes, then mark every answer against the official scheme.
  • Write short process chains from memory, such as how oxygen debt is repaid or how the pupil reflex works, so you can explain and not just name.
  • Track your weak topics from each marked paper and revisit those first, rather than revising what you already know.
  • On the Extended route, give the Supplement content its own revision time, since that is where the A and A* marks are decided.
  • Review older topics in short, spaced bursts so early material does not fade before exam season.

A Term-By-Term Revision Approach

Spread the load across the year instead of cramming. A workable rhythm looks like this:

  • Early in the year, build topic notes as you are taught, keeping definitions in your own words
  • From the second term, add a weekly past-paper section under timed conditions
  • In the final term, target your weakest topics with focused drills rather than re-reading everything
  • Across all three terms, revisit older topics briefly so Year 10 content does not fade by exam season

The breadth of 0610 means gaps form quietly. A topic learned early is easily forgotten, so short, regular review beats one long pass at the end.

How To Handle Diagrams, Magnification, & Data Questions?

Three skills reliably separate strong scripts from average ones. First, diagrams: label clearly, use a ruler for label lines, and be ready to explain how a structure suits its function, not just name it. Second, magnification: learn the formula, magnification equals image size divided by actual size, and practise converting between millimetres and micrometres so units never trip you up. Third, data questions: read the graph before the question, describe the trend in plain terms, then use the figures to support your conclusion.

These are exactly the problem-solving and experimental skills that pure memorisation misses, and they appear across both the theory and practical papers.

Exam Technique That Protects Marks

Command words tell you what to do, and misreading them costs easy marks. Describe what you see; explain wants why it happens; suggest wants a sensible answer applied to a new situation. Cambridge lists them in full inside the official 0610 syllabus, and learning them is quick, high-value revision. Match the length of your answer to the marks available, and never leave a structured question blank, since a reasonable attempt often earns something.

Know More About: How To Study For IGCSE? A Smarter 2026 Method

Ignite – Cambridge IGCSE Biology Tutors In Dubai

Most students do not struggle with biology itself. They struggle with the breadth of the syllabus and the jump from recall to application that Paper 4 demands. That gap is what structured tutoring closes. Sessions at Ignite are built around the real 0610 papers, so students practise the exact question types they will face, with feedback tied to the mark scheme wording.

Our Biology tutors in Dubai focus on the areas where grades are usually decided: precise definitions, diagram and data questions, and the Supplement content that Extended students need for the top grades. One student we supported moved from a shaky start across the sciences to A* results in biology at both IGCSE and A Level, built on steady past-paper practice rather than last-minute cramming.

For families weighing up support across the wider curriculum, our IGCSE tutors in Dubai cover biology alongside other subjects, which helps students balance revision as exams approach. The aim is measurable progress, with each student clear on their next step.

FAQs

1. Is Cambridge IGCSE Biology Hard?

It is manageable with the right preparation, though its breadth makes it feel demanding. The main challenge is the volume of content across 21 topics and the application questions on Paper 4, which reward understanding over memorisation. Students who practise past papers under timed conditions and learn precise definitions usually find the difficulty fair by exam day.

2. How Many Papers Are There In Cambridge IGCSE Biology?

Six papers exist, but every student sits only three. Core students take Papers 1, 3, and either 5 or 6. Extended students take Papers 2, 4, and either 5 or 6. Together they cover multiple choice, theory, and a practical component.

3. What Is The Difference Between Core And Extended In IGCSE Biology?

Core covers the foundation content and caps at grade C. Extended adds the Supplement material and opens up grades A* to C. Core students sit Papers 1 and 3, while Extended students sit Papers 2 and 4. You cannot mix the two routes.

4. Which Coursebook Is Best For Cambridge IGCSE Biology?

The most widely used is the endorsed Cambridge University Press coursebook, currently the fourth edition by Mary Jones and Geoff Jones. It is matched to the 0610 syllabus and suitable for the 2026 to 2028 cycle. Collins and other publishers also produce endorsed alternatives.

5. Where Can I Find Cambridge IGCSE Biology Coursebook Answers?

The answers to the Cambridge coursebook questions are published free on the Cambridge GO platform. You reach them with the code inside the book or through your school. This is the legitimate source, and it is more reliable than unofficial PDFs online.

6. How Do You Get An A* In Cambridge IGCSE Biology?

You need the Extended route, since Core caps at C. Beyond that, an A* comes from precise definitions, strong diagram and data skills, and consistent past-paper practice marked against the official scheme. Reading examiner reports to see where marks are lost helps close the final gap.

7. What Is The Difference Between 0610 And 0970 In IGCSE Biology?

They are the same subject with different grading. Code 0610 is graded A* to G, and code 0970 is graded 9 to 1. The content, papers, and structure are identical, and your school enters you for one code. The two cannot be taken in the same series.

8. How Many Marks Do You Need To Pass Cambridge IGCSE Biology?

There is no fixed pass mark. Cambridge sets grade boundaries after each series, based on how students performed on that specific paper, so the mark for any grade shifts slightly each session. Always check the official boundary table for your exact exam series rather than assuming a set percentage.

9. When Are The Cambridge IGCSE Biology Exams Held?

Cambridge runs exams in the June and November series worldwide, with an additional March series in India. Most Dubai schools enter students for the June session at the end of Year 11. Results are released a few weeks after each series.

10. Can You Use A Calculator In Cambridge IGCSE Biology?

Yes. Cambridge states that calculators may be used in all parts of the exam. You will need one for calculations such as magnification, percentages, and rates, and you should always show your working so method marks are protected.

11. How Many Topics Are In The Cambridge IGCSE Biology Syllabus?

The 0610 syllabus covers 21 topics, from characteristics of living organisms and cell structure through to inheritance, ecology, and genetic modification. Each topic has Core content, and Extended students study additional Supplement material within the same topics.

12. Has The Cambridge IGCSE Biology Syllabus Changed For 2026?

Not significantly. The current syllabus is version 2, published December 2025, for exams in 2026 to 2028. Cambridge confirms there are no significant changes that affect teaching, and textbooks endorsed from 2023 remain suitable. Always confirm you are using the syllabus for your exam year.

Conclusion

Cambridge IGCSE Biology becomes far less intimidating once you can see its shape. One syllabus split into Core and Extended, three papers per student, 21 topics with a human-biology focus, and grades set against each series rather than a fixed line. Knowing that structure early lets you revise with purpose instead of guessing.

Lean on the official resources. Download real past papers, check your answers against the mark scheme, and read a couple of examiner reports before your mocks. Those habits move grades more than any last-minute effort. Precise language and steady data practice are what carry students from a C to an A.

If your child wants structured support built around the real 0610 paper, you can book a free demo class with Ignite and see how a focused plan looks for their target grade.
